questions.stem: A metal spoon left in a hot cup of soup quickly becomes hot to touch, while a wooden spoon does not. What explains this difference?

options.text: Metal absorbs more heat from the soup
Metal is a better conductor of heat because it contains free electrons that transfer energy rapidly
Wood is colder than metal
Metal spoons are thinner than wooden spoons

questions.explanation: Metals are excellent thermal conductors because they contain free (delocalised) electrons. These electrons gain kinetic energy from the hot end and move rapidly through the metal, transferring energy by colliding with other particles. Wood has no free electrons and conducts heat poorly (it is an insulator). Both spoons are at the same initial temperature.

questions.stem: In conduction through a non-metallic solid, how is thermal energy transferred?

options.text: By free electrons moving through the material
By particles vibrating and passing energy to neighbouring particles
By convection currents within the solid
By electromagnetic radiation between particles

questions.explanation: In non-metals, there are no free electrons. Instead, heated particles vibrate more vigorously and collide with their neighbours, passing on kinetic energy. This particle-to-particle transfer is slower than free electron transfer, which is why non-metals are generally poor conductors. Convection cannot occur in solids because particles cannot flow.

questions.stem: Double-glazed windows have a gap filled with air or argon between two panes of glass. How does this reduce heat loss by conduction?

options.text: Glass is a very good conductor, so two layers conduct less
The gas in the gap is a poor conductor because its particles are far apart
The two panes of glass reflect heat back inside
The gap creates a vacuum that prevents all heat transfer

questions.explanation: Gases are poor thermal conductors because their particles are far apart, making particle-to-particle energy transfer very slow and inefficient. The trapped gas layer acts as an insulator. The gap is not a vacuum (it contains gas). Glass is actually a relatively poor conductor too. Reflection of infrared radiation is a separate mechanism (relevant to low-emissivity coatings, not the gas gap).

questions.stem: A student tests four rods made of different materials by coating them with wax and heating one end. The wax melts fastest on the copper rod. What does this show?

options.text: Copper has the highest specific heat capacity
Copper has the highest thermal conductivity
Copper has the lowest melting point
Copper produces the most thermal radiation

questions.explanation: The wax melting fastest on copper shows that thermal energy is conducted most quickly through copper. This means copper has the highest thermal conductivity of the materials tested. A high SHC would mean copper heats up slowly (the opposite). The melting point of copper is irrelevant; it is the wax that melts. Radiation is not the main transfer mechanism along a solid rod.

questions.stem: Why are saucepan handles often made of plastic or wood rather than metal?

options.text: Plastic and wood are cheaper than metal
Metal handles would melt at cooking temperatures
Plastic and wood are poor thermal conductors (insulators), preventing heat reaching the hand
Plastic and wood are stronger than metal

questions.explanation: Plastic and wood are thermal insulators with low thermal conductivity. They prevent heat from the pan conducting through to the user's hand, avoiding burns. Metal handles would conduct heat rapidly and become too hot to hold. Metals do not melt at cooking temperatures (aluminium melts at 660 degrees C, well above cooking temperatures). Cost and strength are secondary considerations.
